posts.title: Task Master Best Practices, Community Spotlight, New Full Product Flow Teaser
posts.content:
In previous versions, it was recommended to do a Global Install

This has since changed to doing it locally per their docs,

However I find it more consistent to have it done globally

This is done by running `npm install -g task-master-ai`

If you're having issues determining the difference...

Locally, it means you have an `mcp.json` inside of the `.cursor/` folder at the top of your project.

If you're getting errors on the MCP page of Windsurf or Cursor (cursor preferred by taskmaster),

Then you may be missing the `mcp.json` in your global Cursor download.

This can be checked by going to `Users/\[your-username\]/.cursor`

Then you can add a `mcp.json` by running `touch mcp.json`

Make sure it at least has the structure of MCP:
```
{
"mcpServers": {}
}
```

Latest Docs:
[https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master](https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master)

We had a great post by @Reg User (Brian) who shared his workflow on Discord last night

I’ve also built similar systems before. At a food delivery startup, we partnered with Google to show up natively in “Chinese food near me” results. We worked with Google X to structure our data, and the result was a 15% lift on a $50M run rate—just from reducing friction.

I’ll be watching this closely. I want to rank for keywords like “vibe marketing” and “AI coding.” You won’t rank for broad terms like “agent,” but long-tail keywords are winnable—and valuable.

posts.title: How to make sure Task Master swims between the flags.
posts.content:
I was watching one of @Parker Rex daily upload videos when he reminded me to read the PRD. I have a confession. I use Gemini, Grok and ChatGPT as text expanders. I can give it a rough idea, and it expands into a beautiful PRD like magic. I don't always read the output... I skim through it.

How often do you read your PRD or ALL that AI generates for you? You are not alone. But what if you paid a team $50,000 to develop the feature or system that you want Task Master to assist you with? Would you read the PRD? Would you cut unnecessary features? I would be more diligent about cutting out fluff.

Assigning a monetary value to PRDs sounds like a hack. However, I will use it for now until I discover a better way of putting guardrails (flags) on Task Master.

"Swim between the flags" is a safety message, particularly in Australia, which encourages swimmers to swim within designated areas marked by red and yellow flags on patrolled beaches. This area is supervised by lifeguards and surf lifesavers, making it the safest place to swim.

One Australian prime minister went swimming outside the flags and was never found! [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disappearance_of_Harold_Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disappearance_of_Harold_Holt)

I know you @Parker Rex have an upcoming video on planning and PRDs. Please consider helping us create PRDs that avoid scope creep. Who said your job is easy? :-)

posts.title: On Writing with AI (dont sound like a bot ❤️ 🤖)
posts.content:
I've been writing with AI for a while

For short copywriting, you can get away with OpenAI models or Gemini models

Anything mid-long form, Anthropic is the absolute king

Otherwise you sound like a straight-up bot

which makes you look worse than saying anything at all

My process:

1> Use ChatGPT Companion for short things using this:
`!gptconcise`

This pops open a snippet tied to a keyboard shortcut ([lesson here](https://www.skool.com/troublefreeai/classroom/4576e8a2?md=53d8a2aa05884476951fac6a4e367d14))

It looks like the screenshot attached

2> Use playgrounds for optimizing writing prompts...
There's levels to using AI
Jr AI guy/gal: uses web browser for everything
mid ai guy/gal: uses a project with custom instructions or Gemini AI Studio
Pro AI guy/gal: understand the POWER of playgrounds

Why playgrounds?
They have prompt optimization tools built in

There's a platoon of ppl who are paid $1m/yr TC to make this button awesome

Use the awesome button

wield the billions going into this space

[googles playground](https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/studio/multimodal?invt=AbtuUQ&project=automations-457120&supportedpurview=project)
[anthropics playground](https://console.anthropic.com/workbench/a5b49029-1056-49b3-9ff5-d22c12e2b721)

BUT PARKER PLAYGROUND HARD ( >,< ) 😡

There are a few toggles - you ignore most.

Temperature = level of creativity

Low temp = don't get creative, be objective, high temp = get crazy with it. highest temp = hallucination

top p = ignore

model = pick the best one (SOTA=. state of the art)

What's the best one?

their most expensive one (for one-off personal writing - don't light $$$ on fire with big repetitive tasks)

If u DID, however, want to turn it into a writing saas... that's a different story and possible while not lighting ur precious dollars on fire just DM with details, as I've done this (hint: mold the crumbier model with a ton of evals/prompting)

posts.title: Automating Thumbnail / GFX Creation with Brand JSON Files
posts.content:
You can take a base image and generate a JSON profile.

This profile then guides ChatGPT Native 4o Image Generation to make the exact style you want.

> Start by creating an image - start from scratch or find one that you like and replicate.
> Paste the following prompt to get the JSON output:

```
create a JSON profile. this JSON profile should be a "brand style" profile that extracts data from these static ads so that i can send the JSON to an Al to give it immediate context on how to replicate such ads in a consistent brand style. It shouldn't include specific product data, such as in this case "prime" or anything that's specific to the prime brand... it should include the messaging style, the type of product placement, the branding, the elements, every single detail about how to replicate such ads for a different product.
```
> the output will look something like below (this is the sauce)

Hi my name is Nate and I'm a business owner and software developer based in Japan. I've been thinking a lot about how I can transition from my current business model of consulting and development work into a product based revenue stream. Right now I live with a bit too much anxiety about client budgets, shifting client priorities, and wondering how long the good thing I've got going will last. I've worked hard to cultivate very long term client relationships but changing leadership and client financial performance have made me question how much longer some of these relationships will last.

I'd like to start focusing on leveraging AI to help me develop tools I can use for my own interests and products that I can sell to change the dynamics of how I'm making money. I'd like to replace my current income before transitioning full-time away from the career I've built over the last 10-12 years.

I'm hear to learn, collaborate, and work hard on improving my knowledge of and skill using AI tools to accomplish these goals. Thanks in advance!

posts.title: Hello from the UK Southwest!
posts.content:
Hey everyone, I'm Sam – a developer, dad of two,sorry, three kids (2-7 years old), dog owner, ex-mountain biker, ex-club dj, ex-muay-thai-er, still football/soccer player and lifelong hip-hop and dance music fan based in the southwest of the UK. I obviously didnt write all of this post - just garbled a load of stuff into Claude and asked it to make it somewhat readable! If its boring you can blame Anthropic.

TLDR: Developer with data/back-end background pivoting to AI-assisted web development for small businesses. Excited about using AI to create comprehensive tech solutions rather than just websites, and looking to connect with like-minded pragmatic AI enthusiasts.

My Developer Journey
My professional path has been quite the evolution. I started in data, gradually moved into back-end Python development, and recently I've been diving into front-end work with the goal of building complete, end-to-end solutions.
I've always considered myself somewhat unconventional as a developer. While I might not be the quickest coder or the most technically inclined with lower-level details, I've consistently relied on strong instincts and sound architectural decision-making. This approach has led to both significant successes and a few challenging setbacks, including a couple of tough job losses.

Pivoting to Local Business Solutions
These career fluctuations ultimately pushed me to reconsider my path. I decided to focus on working directly with small local businesses, which sparked my journey into comprehensive web development. I wanted to understand not just the coding aspects, but everything that makes a website effective – messaging, imagery, sales strategy, and copywriting.
During this transition, I experimented with various platforms before settling on Webflow. I also began leveraging ChatGPT for copywriting, section planning, and coding questions.

The Limitations of No-Code & My AI Epiphany
While Webflow was enjoyable to use, I soon discovered its limitations with more complex functionality. As a back-end engineer, I found myself frustrated when tasks that should have been straightforward became unnecessarily complicated. The platform often required workarounds, and I felt constrained by the layer between myself and the underlying code.
